doc.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Hickory House, Joe Marsala and Nick's
summary: He heard Joe Marsala's band with harpist Adele Girard at the Hickory House and found Nick's cheap and easy to enter.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You learned the tallest drink to get. The bartender would leave you alone. So now that meant, Hickory House for example okay, Hickory House mid to late-30s, I’m listening to Joe Marsala, who not infrequently would have Bud Freeman, Dave Tough, and hey it was a long time before I realized that not every jazz band had a harpist in it. It was Joe’s wife.

Adele Girard played harp and was usually part of his band. But and then I discovered Nick’s and the whole point was also, see you could get in, a high school kid could get in there pretty easily, it was very inexpensive. It got to be, perhaps the music was secondary and in fact what a great place for a cheap date. So I do remember that that was part of the picture.
